title: The Open window in the hall
subtitle: 国家公民 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）
meta: 主题语境：国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）　|　核心词汇：open　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 open 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the tailor wrote of ① an open window in the hall in the order, and everybody in the shop said at once that it was ② more open than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the tailor, who never explained anything, had done it before dawn and gone home; it was the open ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most open window in the hall anybody in the shop had ever seen, or so the order for November 1954 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too open to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the customer who had come to help; the open ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an open meeting of the council, and said that no customer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as open as the meeting of the council they had once had in the old shop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was open or not, and he said so.

By 1967 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the order. What the line asked for was ⑦ something open, and nothing besides. The customer from the next shop called the whole plan ⑧ quite open; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the order kept the names of the open ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1970, in public, she wrote of another open window in the hall in the same order, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ more open than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most open meeting of the council in the whole shop, she said in 1972, was the one she could never quite name; the open ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 开着（前置定语 an open window in the hall：1960 年裁缝在订单簿里记下的那件开着的窗）
B. adj. 开着／公开（比较级 more open than：文中两处，一处比厅里开着的窗，一处比预想）
C. adj. 开着／公开（最高级 the most open：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 开着（表语 too open to do：母亲觉得它太开着，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 公开（前置定语 an open meeting of the council：叔叔把整件事称作一桩公开的会议）
F. adj. 公开（同级比较 as open as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩议会公开举行的会议相比）
G. adj. 公开（后置定语 something open：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 公开（受程度副词修饰 quite open：那位顾客的评价）

items.q: an open window in the hall
the most open window in the hall anybody
an open meeting of the council
The most open meeting of the council in

answers.why: open 意为“开着”，1960 年裁缝在订单簿里记下的是“一件开着的窗”，此处作前置定语 an open window in the hall。
open 意为“开着”，此处用比较级 more open than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
open 意为“开着”，订单簿上 十一月 那行字说它是裁缝铺里最开着的一件，故用最高级 the most open window in the hall。
open 意为“开着”，母亲认为这件东西“太开着了，谁也用不上”，too open to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
open 意为“公开”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩公开的会议”，此处作前置定语 an open meeting of the council。
open 意为“公开”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩议会公开举行的会议一样公开”，同级比较用 as open as。
open 意为“公开”，订单簿上那半行字要的是“公开的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something open。
open 意为“公开”，邻裁缝铺来的那位顾客认为这套计划“相当公开”，quite 修饰原级 open。
open 意为“公开”，1970 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要公开”，故用比较级 more open than。
open 意为“公开”，母亲 1972 年说的是“整个裁缝铺里最公开的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most open meeting of the council。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1960 年，裁缝在订单簿里记下了一件开着的窗。（an open window in the hall）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更开着。（more open than …）
母亲觉得它太开着，谁也用不上。（too open to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩公开的会议。（an open meeting of the council）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩议会公开举行的会议一样公开。（as open as …）
到了 1967 年，订单簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件公开的东西。（something open）
answers: In 1960 the tailor wrote of an open window in the hall in the order.
Everybody said it was more open than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too open to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an open meeting of the council.
He said nobody would call it as open as the meeting of the council they had once had.
By 1967 the order asked for nothing but something open.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 open 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1960 the tailor wrote of an open window in the hall in the order, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most open window in the hall in the shop, or so the order says.
My mother thought it too open to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an open meeting of the council, and nobody argued with him.
The customer from the next shop called the plan quite open, and everybody laughed.
The open ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
